title: A/B results taken at host load >6 are not comparable to the A/A floor; add a per-run load guard (keep chrome-measure at 1 slot)
sig: err:same unchanged baseline: ><n> ms frames median <n> at load<n><<n> (n=<n>) vs <n>-<n> at load<n> <n>-<n> (n=<n>); fps <n> vs <n>-<n>
error: same unchanged baseline: >20 ms frames median 66 at load1<6 (n=11) vs 96-103 at load1 6-15 (n=32); fps 74 vs 67-69
output: Evidence: research/measurement-parallelism (branch of measure-parallel). Retrospective over 11 mobile-6x sessions (98 runs): baseline-side >20 ms frames jump from ~66 (load1<6) to ~96-103 (load1 6-15), LoAF 259->~330 ms; step, not linear. Within one ABBA session the effect is small (r=0.13), so deltas mostly survive but the floor comparison does not. Parallel A/A (c=1/2/3 simultaneous verify, 3 runs each) could not be run clean: background npm test suites pushed load1 to 26-60. c=2 kept per-process medians within 1 fps and 0 A/A false positives; c=3 drove host CPU to 95-100 % (kernel ticks), memory pressure to 'warn', decompressions 238->3919/s, one stalled run (fps 14, LoAF 2 s) and A/A false positives in 3/3 processes. loadavg on macOS overstates CPU (load 40 at 45 % CPU): memory stalls count; ps per-pid deltas missed ~30 % CPU from short-lived test processes. PROPOSAL: (1) keep chrome-measure at N=1 (no semaphore until a clean c=2 A/A at load<6 proves equivalence); (2) verify.mjs records per run: loadavg1, host CPU % from os.cpus() tick deltas during the scroll phase, free memory / compressor; (3) fix.mjs ab marks results.json 'contaminated' (and prints it next to the verdict) when any run starts at load1>10 or host CPU outside the measured Chrome >25 %, warns at load1>6; optional --max-load N that waits (holding the lock) up to 60 s for load to fall before each run; (4) npm test / any CPU job only under the lock (short lane), never alongside a holder.

title: gesture tool's inspector connection hangs when a second inspector connection (morph-log hook) closes; 0 strokes
sig: err:gesture-run: <n> strokes after hook connection closed (<n> reproductions, iphone-runner)
error: gesture-run: 0 strokes after hook connection closed (3 reproductions, iphone-runner)

history.note: C-014 (lead 18:4xZ): the user's Mac Safari Web Inspector was attached to the phone in parallel, likely cause of the inspector wedges (a second inspector connection); closed 18:41:48Z. ts-iphone-run reproduced the hang on the Simulator (iwdp closes the run's connection with ws 1001 when a 2nd connection to the same tab closes); fix written (wip fail-fast, gesture wipPage reconnect + idempotent retry, --inject on the run's connection), Sim check queued.

ts-iphone-run: two mechanisms, both CONFIRMED in source. (1) Another inspector client outside our proxy, e.g. Mac Safari Web Inspector: WebKit RemoteInspectorCocoa.mm receivedSetupMessage ignores a second client's setup while a target has a connection ('if (m_targetConnectionMap.contains(targetIdentifier)) return;'), and receivedDataMessage forwards to the holder's connection, so we see 'no page target' or evaluate timeouts (github.com/WebKit/WebKit main, read 2026-10-01). Fix: a hint in 'no page target', command timeouts and openTab BLOCKED to close that inspector. (2) A second connection through our own proxy (morph-log): ios_webkit_debug_proxy keeps one client per page, the newer takes the page (iwdp_start_devtools 'Taking page ... from local'), and the older's next command is answered with close 1001 'Page N/M claimed by ...' and not forwarded (iwdp_on_frame 'someone stole our page?'; github.com/google/ios-webkit-debug-proxy src/ios_webkit_debug_proxy.c master). Reproduced on the Simulator. Fix: wip.mjs fails fast on close; wipPage reconnects and retries idempotent calls once (run.reconnects); gesture --inject runs the logger on the run's own connection. Simulator check (a second iwdp as the other client) queued; commit and land request follow.
npm test on main (incl. 6a35185 proposals) 886/886 pass. No re-measure (iPhone tooling only).
